question: In a Grand Slam men's singles match, when is a fifth set tiebreak played under current rules?

options.text: Only after 12-12 games in the fifth set
No tiebreak is allowed in the fifth set

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only after 12-12 games in the fifth set**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Grand Slam Men's Singles Matches:** In Grand Slam tournaments like Wimbledon, US Open, Australian Open, and French Open, specific rules govern the fifth set of men's singles matches.
 
• **Introduction of the Fifth Set Tiebreak Rule:** The rule of a tiebreak being played after 12-12 in the fifth set was introduced to prevent matches from dragging indefinitely, ensuring fair competition while managing time constraints.
 
• **Application of the Rule:** Under the current rules, a tiebreak is played **only after both players reach 12-12 games** in the fifth set. This ensures that players still have a chance to win through extended play but avoids excessively long matches.
